findings: Command-local snapshots run inside a fresh nested host callback and use one native-stack lease. Saved handles are traced through the runtime registry private host-state chain.

Shared snapshot traversal is reused with a locals-only mode: no shallow global/custom-environment binding snapshots, while upvalue cells and referenced helper functions/table contents retain their existing native policy.

Named command, group, course and update dispatch record the first call to a Lua closure in an active command scope. Native host callbacks own no Lua upvalue cells. No new scope is activated during ordinary preparation/live execution.
Nested scopes merge encountered functions/snapshots into their owner; the outermost scope restores in reverse snapshot order. RNG restores independently at every nesting boundary.
Failed snapshot construction detaches its retained-value table, including errors opening or filling its stack lease. Successful captures remain rooted across callbacks, detached actor fields and GC.
